title: Care management in the nursing buildings is now billed as place of service 32: back it with each facility's Part A list
why: Until November 10, 2026 every care-management line in the five nursing buildings went out as a Medicare Part A skilled stay (place of service 31) and was paid at that rate: $63.28 for the first hour in 2026. For a long-term resident the code is 32, and Medicare allows $142.98 against $80.71 for the first hour and $77.47 against $44.58 for each added half hour. The owner's rule of November 10 bills these lines as 32 from now on; it went live at 11:14 UTC that day (rule version 2026-11-10.4). Care management is billed as a monthly total at month end, so the November lines are the first to carry 32. The rule reads the visit pattern, so the facility's own list is still the proof.
what: Read the feed reports: counts by place of service, and that AdvancedMD stored 32
Get each facility's monthly list of residents in a Part A stay, with dates
Tell the back end whether to keep the safeguard that leaves care management at 31 in a month that looks skilled
impact_basis: From February to September 2026 Medicare paid about 86 first-hour and 71 add-on lines a month in the nursing buildings. At 32 each first-hour line pays $48.82 more and each add-on $25.79 more, about $6,000 a month and $72,000 a year. Lines the safeguard keeps at 31 (about one resident in eight in October) and lines Medicare matches to a Part A stay reduce it, so the range is $50,000 to $70,000 a year. The patient's 20% share rises by about $19 a month per resident. For the past year the same arithmetic gives $60,015 of Medicare payment not claimed; the owner decided not to ask Medicare to reopen paid claims.
horizon: in place since November 10, 2026; first care-management lines at 32 with the November month-end batch
confidence: high on the rates and the line counts; medium on how many lines Medicare will match to a Part A stay

title: Decide what to do with the October visits entered under the other clinician
why: The charge import entered 165 lines the feed names the nurse practitioner on under the physician, and 2 lines the other way. 120 of them are at Medicare, which pays a nurse practitioner's visit at 85% of the physician amount. Most are billed and not yet paid, so they can still be corrected before the money arrives. The 15 lines not yet billed were decided by the owner on November 10, 2026.
what: Decided November 10: of the 15 lines not yet billed (12 never-billed visits), 10 visits move to the nurse practitioner before they are sent and the 2 initial visits stay under the physician
The owner marks any of the other listed visits he performed himself
For the rest the owner decides: corrected claims for the 133 lines billed and not yet paid, and corrected claims or refunds for the 19 paid lines
impact_basis: Up to about $1,400 of Medicare payment more than is owed if nothing is corrected, and 136 visits already billed under a clinician the feed does not name. Correcting them now costs a rebill; leaving them costs a refund and a finding.
confidence: high on the counts; the owner confirms which visits were his

title: Bring in a healthcare attorney before the visit-level audit begins
why: Once a review shows an overpayment, a 60-day clock starts. A review directed by an attorney can be privileged if its results stay with the attorney, and its timing is documented. This applies to the audit of visit levels and advance care planning.
what: Engage the attorney
Have the attorney hire the auditor
Record the date each review starts and the date any overpayment is identified
impact_basis: Keeps a billing problem a refund and not a penalty.

title: Commission an independent audit of visit levels
why: Six families of visit codes sit far above national patterns. In Medicare's 2025 review the practice's most-billed visit code (99233) had a 22.7% improper-payment rate, and the code it bills for every nursing facility admission (99306) had 25.5%. No chart audit is on record.
what: Attorney engages a certified auditor
10 random notes per code family per clinician
Act on the result, then audit quarterly
impact_basis: Protects about $600,000 a year of visit revenue for a few thousand dollars.

title: Finish the coverage refresh and verify every patient monthly
why: The coverage refresh stopped in mid-September after passes by hand on September 5-8 and 23-24, and no routine works the open cards: 349 of 503 Insurance Refresh Board cards were open on November 10, 2026, and 145 charts with money waiting hold $153,124. That day 122 feed visits ($26,373) had no claim: 86 with a payer on the chart that were never sent ($19,405; 84 of them the never-billed visits), 21 with no plan ($4,358) and 15 moved to the patient's balance ($2,610). Coverage and wrong-payer problems are about a quarter of denied visits.
what: Work the open cards, biggest balances and most recent first (136 with nothing left to bill or collect were closed on November 10)
A check-only coverage run on the first of each month, for the patients being billed that month (approved November 10)
List every held visit daily and re-check held charts; a HOLD today is only a label in the check's report and does not stop the claim
impact_basis: The plan's earlier 'one charge in nine has no payer' was the share of feed dollars on charts the insurance check held (counted after the check ran; $23,534 of $211,062, 11.2%), not a share of all charges. Visits that arrived with no open plan on the chart were 138 of 1,037 ($29,286, 13.7% of dollars). The $30,000 to $70,000 is the plan's earlier range. It was built on the 11.2% figure (about $113,000 a year, with a quarter to 60% assumed never collected), which measured something else. It has not been worked out again and is a placeholder until these visits are tracked to payment. The monthly run adds about $10 to $40 a month of checks and a one-time catch-up of at most about $260. At the plan's median payment of about $45 to $125 a visit, it pays for itself if it saves one visit a month from denial (estimates).
horizon: the cards now; the monthly run once it is built (its build started on November 11, 2026, after rule version .7 went live; the look-up savings went live on November 10)
confidence: low on the dollar range; high on the counts

title: Send the 84 never-billed feed visits as the owner approved, now that the fix is live
why: 84 feed visits ($18,802 of charges, service dates October 12 to November 7, 2026) could never bill, because their insurance-order list was empty: the insurance check had released 69 and held 15. The owner approved the remedy on November 10, 2026 ('yes to all your recommendations').
what: The fix (rule version 2026-11-10.7) is live since November 11, 2026: send one pilot visit and read it back
Send the 71 visits whose payer only the look-up found only when an eligibility check dated to the service date shows the plan active; the two-plan chart by that check; send the other 13
Move the 10 nurse practitioner visits to her before they go; keep the 2 initial visits under the physician
impact_basis: Not valued: the charges are $18,802, but whether each payer found is right is not yet tested. The dated checks cost about $10 to $25.
horizon: now that rule version .7 is live (November 11, 2026); one pilot visit first
confidence: high on the cause and the count; the dated coverage check settles each payer

title: Get skilled-stay, hospice and plan status from each facility every week
why: That status decides the payer, the place of service and the rate. Since November 10, 2026 the back end sets place of service from the visit pattern: the monthly visit as 32, weekly visits and admissions as 31. A facility's own list of Part A stays is the proof behind every 32, and it is what Medicare's own check uses.
what: Monthly or weekly list from each facility: who is in a Part A stay, from when to when
Compare each month's claims billed as 32 with it
Hospice status flagged automatically; the clinician chooses the modifier
impact_basis: For visits the two codes pay differently only in 2026. If every Medicare-paid nursing visit from January to October 2026 had been a long-term resident, Medicare would have paid at most $16,383 more ($20,897 allowed; most of these visits are the nurse practitioner's, paid at 85%). Before go-live the rule was expected to give 32 to about a third of visits; the first live batch gave it to 24 of 31 nursing facility visits. For November 10 to December 31, 2026 that is worth about $1,000 to $3,000 of Medicare payment (estimate). From January 1, 2027 Medicare pays these visits the same under either code. The lasting value is proof for the care-management lines and fewer wrong-payer denials, which are not valued here.

title: File the Medicaid renewal now and clear the enrollment list
why: The physician's Florida Medicaid provider agreement expires December 27, 2026; it is to be filed by November 13 to leave the agency time; December 1 is the last call. Without it, Medicaid and its managed care plans can stop paying the physician and can deny services he orders for Medicaid patients. Those payers are about 6% to 9% of charges. The nurse practitioner's Medicaid enrollment is a new application that was returned with three faults.
what: Reset the Medicaid portal password, then file and confirm the renewal
Resubmit the nurse practitioner's new Medicaid application and correct her national record
Stop writing off Railroad Medicare claims: it paid $718.76 in 2026 and $3,764 is open
impact_basis: Medicaid and Medicaid-plan payments kept and credentialing denials avoided.
horizon: Medicaid by November 13 (December 1 at the latest), the rest by January 31

title: Work the aged receivables before filing deadlines pass
why: $342,620 is open and 35.4% is older than 90 days. $65,431 was tagged as fixable on October 16. Refresh that figure before starting.
what: Sort by filing deadline
Fix and resend, appeal where needed
Report weekly
impact_basis: One-time cash, at about 40% of billed charges on the items worked.

title: Match every deposit to a remittance each week
why: Deposits arrived with no remittance and remittances with no money. Nobody outside the posting process checks the bank.
what: Explain the unmatched items
Finish electronic payment enrollment
Accountant reconciles monthly
impact_basis: One time. The $12,902 of unmatched Medicare deposits is cash already received that could not be posted. The amount on remittances with no deposit has not been totaled, so the range is a placeholder.

title: Close the books monthly and hold a monthly owner review
why: Statements arrive quarterly, there is no budget, and no meeting ties billing, finance and compliance together.
what: Monthly close by the 15th
2027 budget with four scenarios
A 45-minute review with decisions logged
impact_basis: No direct dollar value. It keeps the other gains.

title: Adopt a short written compliance program
why: A working program is what lets a practice show an error was caught in good faith.
what: Write it with the attorney
Review the medical director agreements and time logs
Security risk analysis and vendor list
impact_basis: Changes how any future billing problem is treated.

title: Report 2026 to Medicare's quality program and avoid most of a cut of about 9% in 2028
why: For 2025 nothing was reported: the nurse practitioner's Medicare payments are cut 9% in 2027 and the physician's 1.1%. For 2026 the physician is no longer scored on the hospital's results, so both face about 9% in 2028 unless something is submitted. One attested improvement activity is worth 30 points and unlocks the bonus for complex patients, which was 10 points for each clinician in 2025; the 2026 amount is not known. Rule version 2026-11-10.6, live since 22:46 UTC on November 10, 2026, adds the advance care plan code from the next feed import, up to three lines first; M0004 follows once one of them is seen billed. No line had been entered by the end of November 10 (UTC).
what: Advance care plan code on Medicare claims through December 31 (billing adds it automatically)
M0004 once on one claim for each clinician (billing adds it after the first coded line is seen billed)
Name one improvement activity both clinicians really carried out 90 days in a row in 2026, build its proof file, and attest between January 4 and March 31, 2027
impact_basis: Medicare Part B for the two clinicians is projected at $567,280 for 2026 (range $522,000 to $597,000; the method missed by up to 9% on earlier years). A 9% cut on that is about $47,000 to $54,000; the 9% is itself an estimate (9% if each cost score is 62.5 or lower, about 6.3% at a median cost score). Attesting one activity alone brings the estimated score to about 56 and the cut to about 2.2%, saving about $35,000 to $40,000. Under the neurological option, with the code on 2026 claims, M0004 on one claim for each clinician and the activity, the estimate is at least 69 points and 95 if cost is not scored; 75 or more means no cut. Estimates: the 56 assumes a cost score of 54 and the same 10-point bonus as 2025.
horizon: codes now through December 31; attestation January 4 to March 31, 2027
confidence: high on the rules and dates; medium on the 2026 cost score

title: Restart wellness visits and add transitional care
why: Long-term residents qualify for a yearly wellness visit, and patients discharged home or to assisted living qualify for transitional care. Neither is being billed.
what: About a dozen wellness visits a month
Transitional care routine for discharges
Time statement in advance care planning notes by December 4, 2026 (tracked with the coding audit)
impact_basis: About 150 wellness visits ($137 each, $174 for a first one) and 50 transitional care services ($218 or $295) a year at 2026 Florida Medicare amounts, 15% less when the nurse practitioner bills. A transitional care service includes its follow-up visit, so it replaces a visit worth about $133 where one would have been billed. 2027 amounts are 2% to 5% lower.

title: Collect every payer contract and reprice for 2027
why: No contract is on file, so no payment can be checked. Medicare's 2027 rule cuts the conversion factor 2.31% and changes facility payments.
what: Request contracts and fee schedules
Reprice the top 15 codes for 2027
Flag underpayments automatically
impact_basis: Underpayments recovered and wrongly denied hospital visits disputed.

title: Refinance the 13.99% note and clear the owner's loan
why: The note costs about $30,000 a year in interest. Earnings before owner pay cover the yearly loan payments more than seven times. After a market wage for the owner they cover them about 1.1 times, so a lender may see less room than the owner does. The amount the owner owes the corporation has to be dealt with before any sale.
what: Two refinance quotes
A plan for the shareholder loan
Salary review with the accountant
impact_basis: Each point of rate saved is about $1,900 a year on this balance.

title: Put guard rails on the billing agents
why: The agents are an advantage. A wrong rule repeats on every claim, so the rules that change codes, dates, modifiers, diagnoses, places of service, clinicians or balances need a second pair of eyes. On November 10, 2026 reviews found that the charge import had entered 149 October visits under the other clinician, and that the insurance check had logged success on 84 feed visits that could never bill.
what: Pause the automatic write-off of old balances, close open sign-up and replace the shared key
Approval for claim-changing rules, and an independent review of the exact version before it goes live
Monthly sample of 25 actions, the monthly clinician check on entered visits, and the daily list of never-billed feed visits
impact_basis: Lower chance of a systematic error.

title: Reduce dependence on the owner
why: 76.8% of charges and nearly every relationship sit with one person. It is the main risk to revenue and the main discount on price.
what: Emergency plan and covering physician
Second clinician introduced at each site
Relationship records and written agreements
impact_basis: One more point of the multiple, for example from 3 times earnings to 4, is worth one year of earnings after a market wage: about $88,000 on the wage used in the valuation, and up to about $170,000 in the valuation's high case, where a buyer assumes a lower wage and counts all $48,000 of stipends.

title: Add a second nurse practitioner once the audit is done
why: Clinician time limits growth. The current nurse practitioner generated $193,669 of Medicare allowed charges alone in 2024.
what: Map the facilities in reach
Build the case with ramp and enrollment delay
Start enrollment the day the offer is signed
impact_basis: After about $200,000 a year of pay, benefits and costs, at $80 collected per visit and 215 working days: about $30,000 at the current nurse practitioner's pace of 13.4 visits a day, about $90,000 at 17 a day, and a loss below about 12 a day or during the first months. Check the $80 against her actual collections before deciding.

title: Build the file a buyer would ask for
why: A buyer pays for earnings it can verify. Monthly statements, contracts and a clean audit turn claimed earnings into proven ones.
what: Data room folder
Recurring collections separated from one-time recovery
Yearly valuation refresh
impact_basis: Each $100,000 of proven earnings is worth about $300,000 of price.
